messages.content: Find a pet-friendly train station in Miami

function.name: find_hotel
function.description: Search for hotels based on specific criteria like price range and pet policy. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city where you want to book the hotel.

max_price_per_night.description: The maximum amount you are willing to pay per night. This is a float type value.

pet_friendly.description: Whether the hotel should allow pets. Defaults to false.

message.content:
I’m not aware of any official “pet‑friendly” designation for train stations themselves—most stations simply allow pets on the trains that depart from them, subject to the carrier or leash rules of the rail operator. In Miami, the main intermodal hub is the **Miami Intermodal Center** (formerly known as Miami Central Station). It’s the only major passenger rail station in the city and serves Amtrak’s Silver Service (Silver Meteor/Silver Star) and the Brightline high‑speed rail line. **Key points for bringing pets from this station:** | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Location** | 1 SE 1st Street, Miami, FL 33131 | | **Rail services** | Amtrak Silver Meteor/Silver Star, Brightline | | **Pet policy on trains** | • Pets are allowed on board Amtrak and Brightline, but must be in a carrier or on a leash.
• Only one pet per passenger is permitted, and the carrier must fit under the seat or in the luggage area.
• Pets must be well‑behaved and not disturb other passengers. | | **Station amenities** | The station itself doesn’t have dedicated pet facilities (e.g., pet relief areas), but it’s fully accessible for passengers with pets. | | **Nearby pet services** | If you need a place to walk your dog before boarding, the station is close to several parks and pet‑friendly cafés in downtown Miami. | So while the station isn’t officially labeled “pet‑friendly,” it is the primary point of departure for trains that do allow pets, and it’s designed to accommodate passengers traveling with their animals. If you’re planning a trip, just remember to bring a suitable carrier or leash and check the specific train’s pet policy ahead of time.
